newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MEDIA LAW CHANGE LOBBYING CONTINUES
Federal Communications Minister, Richard Alston, is continuing attempts to convince Coalition backbenchers of the need for changes to Australia's media ownership rules.
Senator Alston held another meeting late last night with the Government's backbench communications committee, during which options for rule changes were canvassed.
Coalition MPs have expressed concern any attempt to scrap cross-media ownership laws could reduce media diversity, and they want to be fully consulted about any changes Cabinet is considering.
Committee chairman, Gary Hardgrave, says he's pleased with last night's meeting and discussions with the Minister will continue.
Cabinet is expected to finalise media law reform within the next month.
PRIVATE EYE URGED TO CONTACT POLICE OVER KIDNAP CASE
Police are appealing for a private detective with information on the disappearance of Kerry Whelan to contact them again.
Mrs Whelan disappeared from a Parramatta car park three weeks ago.
Her husband received a ransom demand for a million dollars, but the ransom deadline has now passed.
Police say the private detective rang a hotline with useful information about the mother of three's disappearance, but they urgently need to talk with him again.
The police hotline has received about 500 calls from the public since being set up last week.
NSW ELECTRICITY SELL-OFF OPPOSITION STILL STRONG
In New South Wales, Power industry unions will conduct a major industrial and political campaign to fight a government proposal to privatise the state's electricity industry.
A meeting of electricity generation and distribution unions in Sydney last night unanimously agreed to oppose the 22-billion dollar sell-off.
The Labor Council says it's confident they can convince the community the industry should not be privatised, and will be lobbying members of parliament for support.
Industrial Officer, John Robertson, says unions are calling on the Premier to withdraw the proposal.
COMMISSION WELCOMES PASSING ON OF FULL INTEREST RATE CUT
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has welcomed yesterday's move by the ANZ Bank to pass on the latest Reserve Bank interest rate cut to its customers in full.
This follow's the half-of-one-percent reduction in the official interest rate, and the subsequent lowering of interest rates by most home-lenders.
Most of the big banks, however, have failed to passed on the full rate cut to consumers.
Head of the A-triple-C, Allan Fels, says competition for mortgages will be looked at when the Commission is asked to approve mergers between financial institutions.
Professor Fels says the response on home-loan interest rate reductions is a factor the commission looks at in any mergers.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
